card.name: Azonto
card.tagline: Communicative Ghanaian street dance and music genre from Accra
card.profile: Azonto is a dance and music genre from Ghana connected to the traditional Ga dance Kpanlogo, associated with coastal Greater Accra towns such as Chorkor, James Town, Teshie, Nungua and Tema (Wikipedia). Several accounts say it was formerly known as 'Apaa' ('work'); its hand movements mimic everyday activities (washing, driving, ironing, praying). One foot is planted while the other pivots on the ball; the hands trace flowing circular motions (Wikipedia). Per Red Bull, following Sarkodie and E.L.'s 2011 'U Go Kill Me', the Azonto craze rapidly took over Ghana and African diaspora communities in the UK and US.
card.insight: Popular-music researcher Jesse Weaver Shipley argues that, like hiplife, Azonto's popularity stems from diaspora interactions - identified with Ghanaian indigeneity by those abroad and with cosmopolitanism by those at home (Wikipedia).
